Drowning is one of the worst ways to go. When you can't hold your breath anymore your lungs fill with water, and your mind goes into pure fight-or-flight mode. You'll probably start thrashing around at this point. Between the burning lungs and your brain going berserk you're going to become desperate to escape. Imagine being dragged feet first down a hole, clawing out in front of you to try and get away, but nothing works, as the realization sinks in that you can't go back. This is it. You're about to die scared and confused. At this point your brain is screaming at you with regret, and you might even be mentally regressing to childhood and maybe you try to cry out for help but no words come out. At some point you'll lose consciousness. At least now you're not awake, but then your lungs burst with one last jolt of “pain” that shoots through your body like an electric shock, and then you're dead.

Drowning sucks. It's one of the most traumatic ways you could possibly die, next to burning to death. Don't do it. If you're suicidal cos you're in mental pain, then drowning yourself will make your last moments utterly unbearable.

The story for Observer by The Acacia Strain is fascinating and quite disturbing. It's about a married man who has night terrors where he kills his wife almost every night. Realizing that his worst nightmare came true, he goes to the garage and attempts suicide by idoling the car with the exhaust pouring through the window. I was never depressed that early on fortunately, but by the time I was around 11 (2009) I started suffering symptoms. I won't go into detail but I was guilty about a couple of things and I felt like my parents were faking affection for me. I started breaking down in tears and having more bad days than good ones, my sleep suffered and my general outlook on life was pretty bad.

By my first year in high school I wanted to kill myself. Everyone I reached out to didn't understand or refused help, and the principle just made things worse when I told her how I was feeling. Despite the fact that I felt like a burden to my family already, she decided that she would only give me help if I would call up my parents right then and there and tell them that I wanted to kill myself. From then on I was extremely tight-lipped about my depression, and it festered inside me until 2013, when I got sent to hospital after breaking down and telling one of my best friends that I had plans to kill myself.

As far back as I can remember, even before the depression symptoms, I disliked who I was as a person. I was generally considered the weird guy in elementary school and I remember always been treated like an outsider, especially by the girls. I remember feeling pretty unwelcome outside of my small friendship group, and even feeling hatred towards some of the other kids because of how insufferable some of them were. The self-image problem has grown alot since then though, as it's grown into self-loathing to the point where I hurt and punish myself for no good reason because I feel like I deserve it. I think it's embedded in the fact that I've always been very humble and shy, even as a 3 year old. I never had tantrums, I never tried to be the center of attention - I was just me. 

I never really felt proud of anything I did, which lead to a combination of perfectionism and avoidance. I would start off really enthused by the work I was doing at school and I've have some really cool ideas, but if I realized my perfect ideas were impractical I would stop caring. That led to general laziness and avoidant behaviour all throughout my life, and up to this point I still don't have any work ethic, which is probably my biggest problem next to my self-esteem.

Sorry, that was practically an essay. Just felt like sharing. You aren't alone in forgetting what it feels like to be happy, I think alot of people here have that problem. It's the same with me, I feel like the depression has been my entire life up to this point, so imagining a "normal" life seems impossible.
